SFFS Critical Development Rules
nodes.rationale: Always run pytest after edits; never commit directly to master; use conventional commits; never hardcode secrets; each student owns their module; OS isolation markers for --secure-required mode; block writes to sffs_data/, security/, .pem, .key files

nodes.label: Three-Student Module Map
nodes.rationale: Three-student team: crypto (code1/), runtime security (code2/), USB/UI/cloud (code3/) — each independently developed, integrated via sffs_core.py

nodes.label: 7-Step Initialization Sequence
nodes.rationale: Initialization order matters: drive detection first (establishes paths), then config, auth DB, audit logger, process monitor, sandbox (post-login), USB removal watchdog

nodes.label: Encrypt Operation Flow
nodes.rationale: Ensure RSA keypair + keystore -> random 32-byte AES key -> encryptFile -> .sffs -> wrapAESKey -> .aeswrap -> generateHash -> audit log. AES key wiped from memory after use.

nodes.label: Decrypt Worker Boundary & Policy
nodes.rationale: isolated_worker.py as dedicated decrypt process; worker_policy.json constrains allowed actions and output root; signed HMAC-SHA256 envelope with short TTL prevents replay; emergency triggers terminate worker processes before global lock

nodes.label: .sffs Binary File Format
nodes.rationale: Custom binary format: magic SFFS + version 0x01 + IV(16) + auth_tag(16) + SHA-256(32) + original_size(8) + ciphertext — enables self-contained encrypted files with integrity verification

nodes.label: SFFS Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Adversaries: malware on host, physical attacker with USB access, network eavesdroppers, local debugging tools. Assumption: OS may be hostile; decrypted files must not land on untrusted host paths. Out of scope: hardware side-channels, full memory forensics, quantum attacks

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM Encryption
nodes.rationale: File confidentiality + integrity in one pass. GCM chosen over CBC because GCM provides authenticated encryption (both confidentiality and tamper detection) whereas CBC only provides confidentiality. GCM tag + stored SHA-256 over plaintext for end-to-end check.

nodes.label: Argon2id Password Hashing
nodes.rationale: Winner of Password Hashing Competition; memory-hard — resistant to GPU and ASIC brute-force; preferred over PBKDF2 or bcrypt for new systems. OWASP 2023 parameters: time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536 (64MB), parallelism=4

nodes.label: Security Regression Test Checklist
nodes.rationale: 6 automated tests in test_worker_hardening.py: signed IPC envelope (valid/forged), replay staleness, worker output confinement, action minimization, path traversal escape guard

nodes.label: OS-Level Isolation v1
nodes.rationale: Linux: AppArmor profile sffs-main-code loaded via aa-exec. Windows: Job Object wrapper with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and active-process cap. Owned under code2/ (Student 2). --secure-required flag fails closed when confinement markers missing

nodes.label: P1 Demo-Killing Bug Fixes
nodes.rationale: NameError in authenticateUser (pw instantiation order) -> timing oracle vuln. UI freeze from sync encrypt/decrypt -> WorkerThread. Hardcoded demo_user prefill removed

nodes.label: P4 Security Fixes
nodes.rationale: Master password moved off CLI args to stdin (visible in ps aux). WrapStore temp file moved inside sandbox (not /tmp). chmod 0o700 on sandbox subdirs

nodes.label: Project Team & Supervisor

nodes.label: 8-Phase Build Plan
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 (Scaffold) -> P1 (Crypto) -> P2 (Security) -> P3 (Architect) -> P4 (Integration) -> P5 (Runners/Tests) -> P6 (Docs) -> P7 (USB Install). Each verified before next.

nodes.label: Post-Build Hardening Plan
nodes.rationale: P1: OS isolation under code2/ ownership; P2: CI quality; P3: .aeswrap hardening (bind metadata, key commitment); P4: hash-chain audit entries, replay-cache; P5: portable USB viewer policy with allowlist

nodes.label: Multi-Layer Security Summary
nodes.rationale: Files: AES-256-GCM; Key wrap: RSA-OAEP; Private key: PBKDF2+AES-GCM keystore; Passwords: Argon2id; Integrity: SHA-256+GCM tag+verifyHash

nodes.label: Developer Guide & Style Rules
nodes.rationale: pathlib.Path for all paths; sensitive passwords as bytearray; no hardcoded drive letters; cross-platform checks; all imports need WHY comments; every function needs Args/Returns/Raises/Security docstrings

nodes.label: Phase 1: Student 1 Crypto Module
nodes.rationale: All 6 crypto functions (f01-f06): RSA key gen, AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt, SHA-256 hash, hash verification, secure key storage. Every file independently runnable with __main__ demo block.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Student 2 Security Module
nodes.rationale: 6 security functions (f07-f12): sandbox, memory wipe, Argon2id auth, process monitor, audit log, emergency lock. Design principle: degrade gracefully — if security op fails, lock down.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Student 3 Architect Module
nodes.rationale: 6 architect functions (f13-f18): USB detection, PyQt6 UI, file manager, cloud sync, config, threads. Key design: importable without display server.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Main Integration
nodes.rationale: Wires all 18 functions via SFFSCore orchestrator. Initialization order, shutdown order, encrypt/decrypt operations, threat/USB callbacks all managed centrally.

nodes.label: Isolated Execution Environment
nodes.rationale: Decrypted data accessible only within the application; prevents host-system malware from reading sensitive data during active file usage

nodes.label: Incremental Development Model
nodes.rationale: Security-critical systems benefit from early prototyping and iterative testing; each increment focuses on a specific module (UI, authentication, encryption, cloud backup); risks identified before full system integration

nodes.label: Isolated Worker Process
nodes.rationale: Sensitive decryption performed outside the main GUI process to enhance security and prevent memory scraping

nodes.label: Emergency Lock
nodes.rationale: On USB removal the app exits, sandbox is destroyed, session terminated; prevents data exposure if drive is physically removed

nodes.label: Constant-Time Comparison
nodes.rationale: Prevents timing attacks when verifying SHA-256 hashes

nodes.label: USB Portable Environment (No Install)
nodes.rationale: System operates without installation or administrator privileges; runs directly from USB for use on untrusted/public computers

nodes.label: Full Cloud Sync (Auto-sync)
nodes.rationale: Not implemented as auto-sync; manual upload/download via Google Drive API only. Deferred due to complexity and potential security risks of background network calls

nodes.label: C++ or Java Backend Modules
nodes.rationale: Not implemented; project remained pure Python for portability and ease of integration across student modules

nodes.label: HSM/YubiKey Support
nodes.rationale: Future work: store master keys on hardware token for multi-factor authentication

nodes.label: Linux Sandbox Hardening (bubblewrap/Firejail)
nodes.rationale: Future work: integrate with bubblewrap or Firejail for stricter OS-level containment
